exercises.title: A counter
exercises.prompt:
This script goes with a page that has

,
exercises.starter: // Find the elements, keep a number, and react to clicks.

tests.check: const a = document.getElementById("add"), c = document.getElementById("count"); a.click(); a.click(); a.click(); if (String(c.textContent) !== "3") throw new Error("after 3 clicks, count shows " + c.textContent);
tests.name: three clicks show 3

tests.check: document.getElementById("reset").click(); if (String(document.getElementById("count").textContent) !== "0") throw new Error("reset should show 0"); document.getElementById("add").click(); if (String(document.getElementById("count").textContent) !== "1") throw new Error("after reset and one click it should show 1");
tests.name: reset works

exercises.title: Live converter
exercises.prompt:
A page has , and

. Write a plain function convert(ksh, rate) giving the dollars as text with 2 decimals plus " USD" ("10.00 USD"; "–" if either isn't a number). Then make every "input" event on ksh show convert(...) in usd.

tests.hint_if_fail: An empty box is Number("") which is 0. Treat empty as not a number.

tests.check: document.getElementById("rate").value = "130"; const k = document.getElementById("ksh"); k.value = "2600"; k.dispatch("input"); if (document.getElementById("usd").textContent !== "20.00 USD") throw new Error("typing 2600 should show 20.00 USD, it shows " + document.getElementById("usd").textContent);
tests.name: updates as you type

hints: Keep convert pure: just numbers in, text out.

quiz.q: Why textContent rather than innerHTML for showing what someone typed?
choices: textContent never runs anything as code, so it's safe
quiz.why: innerHTML with user text is a classic security hole (XSS).

choices: At the end of the body (or with defer)
quiz.why: So the elements exist when the code runs.

quiz.q: Event for every keystroke in a box?
quiz.why: input fires as the value changes.
